A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison. The additional checklist page in v2 contains only a heading.

before.justification: v1 reports original CC-MADDPG experiments in Section 5, including benchmark comparisons, prior comparisons, and ablations, plus agent-count experiments in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix A.2, including Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain identical communication priors, JSD/CLUB mutual-information estimators, reward shaping, and policy-learning procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four MPE tasks under unrestricted, Markov-based, and distance-based communication conditions. Appendix A.2 retains the same Simple_Tag agent-count coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains MAIC, FC-MADDPG, Dropout-MADDPG at rates 0.2/0.5/0.8, and MADDPG. Comparator membership in the prior, ablation, and appendix comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A.1.2 retain identical communication settings, network configurations, training budgets, and evaluation procedures, including four million training steps and 100 evaluation episodes of 25 steps.

E4.justification: The prior comparison in Table 2, dual-mutual-information ablation in Table 3, and scalability analysis in Appendix A.2/Table 4 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 1 and report mean episode rewards and standard deviations over 100 evaluation episodes. No run-count, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-testing changes appear.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 and their accompanying findings are identical. For example, Table 1 reports CC-MADDPG at 138.0±88.1 and FC-MADDPG at 1.5±5.2 for Simple_Tag under heavy distance-based constraints in both versions.

T1.justification: The formal problem definition in Section 3 and mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations 1–8 are unchanged. No proofs or theoretical arguments are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified communication priors, dual mutual-information optimization, and robust multi-agent cooperation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of prior matching, component complementarity, communication robustness, and scalability are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same open questions about value-based extensions and adaptation to highly dynamic environments.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains identical environment descriptions, hardware, architectures, optimizer settings, buffers, and exploration details. The added checklist heading supplies no reproducibility or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research positioning elsewhere, and all 31 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the second affiliation from School of Artificial Intelligence and Science to School of Intelligence Science and Technology, adds funding identifier KG202514, and appends a NeurIPS Paper Checklist heading. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds an otherwise blank final page headed NeurIPS Paper Checklist and slightly reflows the updated affiliation and funding text. Figure 1, Algorithm 1, and Tables 1–4 retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, interpretations, and appendix reproducibility details are unchanged. The affiliation and funding updates are administrative, while the heading-only checklist adds no substantive information; together these edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
